title: Cartesian closedness of the infinity category of spaces
statement: Use the universe and coherent infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of small spaces. The infinity category $\mathcal S$ is cartesian closed: for every small space $X$ there is a coherent functor $\operatorname{Map}(X,-):\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$ and an equivalence of spaces $$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X\times Y,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(Y,\operatorname{Map}(X,Z)),$$ natural in $X$, $Y$ and $Z$, so that $X\times-:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Map}(X,-)$. Empty spaces are allowed.
